interpretation: Changing only input coactivation grouping writes a repeatable pair-specific route-overlap relationship into fixed-budget 3-D material. A fixed distributed local cubic nonlinearity converts that structural relationship into a small but consistent pairwise interaction; soma-only nonlinearity and spatial mass shuffling do not explain the signed effect.
limitations: The normalized pair-interaction program effect is about 0.9 percentage points, not a large task-level effect.
Coactivation produces route separation under this rule; the reason for the sign is unresolved.
An abstract graph can reproduce the effective conductance matrix, so Euclidean 3-D necessity is not established.
Broad parameter robustness has not yet been established.
